title: How to compare money market accounts vs. high-yield savings accounts in the US
description: Understanding the nuances of liquidity, check-writing, and insurance coverage.
content:
When looking for a safe place to park cash, investors often get confused between Money Market Accounts (MMAs), Money Market Funds (MMFs), and High-Yield Savings Accounts (HYSAs). They all seem to do the same thing: pay interest on cash. However, there are critical structural differences regarding insurance (FDIC vs SIPC), access (Check-writing vs Transfer-only), and rate stability. Choosing the wrong one can mean either lower returns or unexpected illiquidity when you need the money most.

Key Takeaways

  • MMA vs HYSA: A Money Market Account (MMA) is a bank product with FDIC insurance, often with check-writing/debit card features. A HYSA usually has no debit card.
  • MMF (Fund): A Money Market Fund is an investment product (SIP insured) bought at a brokerage. It often yields slightly more than bank accounts but is not FDIC insured.
  • The Yield Premium: Historically, MMFs pay slightly higher rates than HYSAs because they invest directly in commercial paper and Treasuries, bypassing the bank's profit margin.
  • Liquidity: If you need to pay rent directly from savings, an MMA is better. If you just want to hoard cash, a HYSA or MMF is fine.

Why It Matters (US Context)

In 2025, Money Market Funds like Vanguard's VMFXX or Fidelity's SPAXX have become the default 'Savings Account' for many savvy investors because they sit inside the brokerage account, allowing for instant deployment into stocks if the market crashes.

The Three Contenders

Which vehicle fits your needs?

1. High-Yield Savings (HYSA)

  • Provider: Online Banks (Ally, Marcus).
  • Insurance: FDIC ($250k).
  • Access: ACH Transfer (1-3 days). No checks.
  • Best For: Emergency Fund you want to keep separate from spending.

2. Money Market Account (MMA)

  • Provider: Banks/Credit Unions.
  • Insurance: FDIC ($250k).
  • Access: Checks / Debit Card (usually limited to 6/month).
  • Best For: People who want yield but might need to write a check for a large purchase (e.g., Down Payment).

3. Money Market Mutual Fund (MMF)

  • Provider: Brokerages (Vanguard, Fidelity).
  • Insurance: SIPC (Protects against fraud, not value loss). *Not FDIC*.
  • Yield: Often highest.
  • Best For: 'Dry Powder' inside your investment portfolio.

How to Choose

  1. The One-Stop Shop: If you want simplicity, open a Fidelity Cash Management account. It sweeps cash into FDIC-insured banks but pays MMF-like rates. It blurs the lines.
  2. The Rate Chaser: If you want the absolute max yield, a MMF (like VMFXX) usually wins by 0.20% - 0.50% over HYSAs.
  3. The Safety Purist: If you are terrified of 'Breaking the Buck' (investments losing value), stick to FDIC-insured HYSAs. MMFs are 99.99% safe, but HYSA is 100% safe.
  4. State Tax Hack: Some MMFs (like VUSXX) invest only in US Treasuries. This income is state-tax free. Bank MMA/HYSA interest is fully taxable. In CA/NY, the MMF wins easily on after-tax yield.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I lose money in a Money Market Fund?

Theoretically yes ('Breaking the Buck'), but it has only happened twice in history (1994, 2008) and regulations were tightened. It is considered 'Cash Equivalent' for a reason.

Why do banks offer MMAs and HYSAs?

Legacy. MMAs used to be the only way to get high rates. Now HYSAs match them. Banks keep both products to segment customers.

What is a Sweep Account?

A feature at brokerages where your uninvested cash is automatically moved into a MMF or FDIC-bank program to earn interest. Always turn this ON.
